description: Wire vectors of the Metadata API (key 3, v0 to v13), replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: Metadata request v0 with an empty topic array, which asks for every topic of the cluster.
Metadata request v0 for one topic; a topic that does not exist yet is created by this request when auto.create.topics.enable is on.
Metadata of a topic with three partitions on a single-broker cluster.
Metadata request v2 for one topic; a topic that does not exist yet is created by this request when auto.create.topics.enable is on.
Metadata of a topic with three partitions on a single-broker cluster, with the cluster id and the controller id of version 2 and a broker without a rack.
Metadata request v2 with a null topic array, which asks for every topic of the cluster, the internal ones included.
Metadata request v2 with an empty topic array, which asks for no topic at all: only version 1 and above can express it.
The answer to a request for no topic: the brokers of the cluster, the cluster id, the controller id and an empty topic array.
Metadata request v1 for one topic; the frame differs from the one of v2 in the version field of the header alone.
The version 1 answer for the same topic: the racks, the controller id and the internal flag are there, the cluster id of version 2 is not.
The metadata of __consumer_offsets, the only topic a 0.10.2.2 broker flags with is_internal.
Metadata request v3 for one topic; the frame is the one of v2, only the version field differs.
Metadata answer v3: the same body as v2, opened by the throttle time that KIP-124 added.
Metadata request v4 with `allow_auto_topic_creation = true`, which is what a consumer or a producer sends.
Metadata answer v4, byte for byte the layout of v3: what version 4 added is a field of the request.
Metadata request v4 with `allow_auto_topic_creation = false` for a topic that does not exist, which is what the AdminClient sends.
The answer to it: the error code 3 (UnknownTopicOrPartition) for the topic, which stays uncreated.

Metadata v5 for one topic, with allow_auto_topic_creation = false. The frame is the one of version 4, byte for byte; what the version states is that the client understands the offline_replicas of the answer.

The answer of that request. Every partition entry ends with the offline_replicas array that version 5 added (KIP-112/113), which is empty on the one-broker container: no replica of the topic is on a broker that is down or on a log directory that failed.

Metadata request v6 for one named topic, with allow_auto_topic_creation = false. The body is the body of version 4, byte for byte - MetadataRequest.json @ 2.8.2 has no field between version 4 and version 8.

Metadata response v6 of the one-broker container: the throttle time, the single broker with its null rack, the cluster id, the controller id and the topic with its partition, whose offline_replicas array of version 5 is empty. The frame is the one of version 5.

Metadata request v7 for one named topic. The body is the body of version 4, byte for byte - MetadataRequest.json @ 2.8.2 has no field between version 4 and version 8 - and what version 7 states is that the client understands the leader_epoch the answer gained.

The answer of that request: the leader_epoch that version 7 (KIP-320) inserted behind the leader id of every partition. It is 0 on this container, the epoch of a partition that has been led by the same broker since it was created; every leader election raises it by one.

Metadata request v8 (Kafka 2.3, KIP-430) for one named topic, with both booleans of the version ON: include_cluster_authorized_operations and include_topic_authorized_operations sit behind the allow_auto_topic_creation of version 4, in that order.

The answer of that request: every topic entry ends with a topic_authorized_operations bitfield, behind its partitions, and the frame ends with the cluster_authorized_operations. A broker without an authorizer - the container has none - answers the full set of the operations of the resource; the bits are the codes of AclOperation @ 2.8.2.

The answer of the same version 8 request with both booleans OFF, which is what this client sends by default: the two bitfields are there - they are fields of the version, not of the question - and carry 80 00 00 00, Integer.MIN_VALUE, "you did not ask". That is not the empty set, which is the bitfield 0.

Metadata request v9 (Kafka 2.4), the first FLEXIBLE version of this api (KIP-482): the request header v2 - the client id as a NON-compact string and a tag buffer of its own behind it - a COMPACT topic array (the unsigned varint 02 for one entry), the topic name as a compact string (0b for ten bytes), the three booleans of the versions 4 and 8 and the tagged-field section of the body. The question is the one of version 8, in the other encoding.

The answer v9: the response header v1 - the correlation id and a tag buffer - then the throttle time, a compact broker array whose entry ends in its own tag buffer, the compact cluster id, the controller id, a compact topic array whose partitions carry compact replica, isr and offline-replica arrays and a tag buffer each, the two authorized_operations bitfields of KIP-430 with Integer.MIN_VALUE ("not asked") and the tagged-field section of the body.

Metadata request v11 (Kafka 2.8, KIP-700), the version this client sends: every topic entry carries the topic_id of KIP-516 IN FRONT of its name - the zero uuid, because the server side of naming a topic by its id is not implemented - and the body ends with allow_auto_topic_creation and include_topic_authorized_operations alone: KIP-700 took include_cluster_authorized_operations out and gave the question to the DescribeCluster api.

The answer v11: the topic entry carries the 16 raw bytes of the topic id between its name and its is_internal flag, and the frame ends with the tagged-field section of the body - there is no cluster_authorized_operations behind the topics any more.
The same question as a version 10 frame, the last one that carries include_cluster_authorized_operations: both booleans of KIP-430 are asked for here, and the topic entry is the same one of KIP-516.

The answer v10: the topic id of KIP-516 in every topic entry, the topic_authorized_operations bitfield behind its partitions and the cluster_authorized_operations at the very end of the frame, in front of the tagged-field section of the body.

Metadata request v12 (Kafka 3.1, KIP-516), the version MetadataRequestV12 keeps: the frame is the version 11 one, field for field - the topic entry carries the zero topic_id in front of its name, because this request names the topic by name - and what version 12 changes is that the server now resolves a topic_id.
The answer v12 of a request by name: the same frame as version 11, with the topic id of the topic between its name and its is_internal flag.

The question KIP-516 wrote the version for: the topic entry carries a real topic id and a NULL name (the compact null 00), which is what describeTopics(TopicCollection.ofTopicIds(...)) of the Java admin client sends. The versions 10 and 11 carry the same two fields and the server ignores them.

What the node answers it: the entry of the resolved topic, with its NAME filled in - an answer never leaves the name out for a topic it could resolve - so this frame is byte for byte the answer of the request by name, except for its correlation id.
The same question with a topic id the cluster does not host, 16 bytes of 0x7f.

The answer that the nullable name of version 12 exists for: the topic entry carries the error code 100 UnknownTopicId, the id that was asked for, a NULL name (the compact null 00 where a name would be) and no partition at all. The brokers of the cluster are reported as usual.
One request that names one topic by its id and another one by its name: the two entries of the array carry the two shapes next to each other, the id of the first and the compact name of the second.

What the node really answers: the topic that was named by its ID, and that one alone. KafkaApis @ 3.9.2 sets useTopicId as soon as ONE entry carries a non-zero id and then serves the ids of the request and nothing else (handleTopicMetadataRequest: topics = knownTopicNames), so the entry that named its topic by name is dropped without a word. A client asks by id or by name, never in one request.
The same by-id question asked with version 11, which MetadataRequest.json @ 3.1.2 says must not be asked ("Versions 10 and 11 should not use the topicId field or set topic name to null").

What the node answers it: not the topic, but a whole ERROR response - zero brokers, a null cluster id, the controller id -1 and one topic entry with the error code 42 InvalidRequest, an empty name and the id that was asked for. An empty broker array is what this client reads as "the metadata cache is not filled yet", so a version below 12 must never be asked by id.

Metadata request v13 (Kafka 4.0, KIP-1102) for one named topic, without auto creation and without the authorized operations: the version 12 body with the version 13 in its header - MetadataRequest.json @ 4.0.0 adds no field and only comments "Version 13 supports top-level error code in the response".

The answer v13 of the kafka-4-3-1 node: the version 12 answer - the one broker 1 at 127.0.0.1:9092, the cluster id, the controller 1 and the topic with its id, its one partition led by 1 at the epoch 0 and the Integer.MIN_VALUE of operations nobody asked for - followed by the two bytes of the top-level error_code of KIP-1102, 0, in front of the tag buffer of the body.
The same question for a topic that does not exist, still without auto creation.

The refusal lives in the topic entry - the 3 UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION with the zero topic id and no partition - and the top-level error_code stays 0. No broker of Kafka 4.0 to 4.3.1 writes a code there: MetadataRequest.getErrorResponse @ 4.3.1 puts the code of a failed request into every topic entry, and the 129 REBOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED the field exists for is read by the clients alone (NetworkClient and KafkaAdminClient @ 4.3.1).
